Chapter 9: Proactively Creating Opportunities
You know, opportunities almost never show up with a bright label or a formal invitation. More often than not, they slip in as small openings, quick moments, or even problems just waiting for someone to solve.
So many people sit back, hoping the perfect chance will find them, or that someone will finally see what they’re capable of. But here’s the thing—when you’re the one who steps up, who looks for ways to add value, you’ll find that doors start opening in the most unexpected places.
Let me share a story. There’s a college student who’s dreaming of breaking into a tough industry. She doesn’t just wait for job postings to appear. Instead, she digs deep into companies she admires, and she reaches out directly, offering to help on real projects. Sure, most don’t even reply. But a few do. And just one conversation leads to an internship, which later becomes a full-time job. Her path isn’t a straight line—it’s one she carves out herself.
Or think about a young professional who spots a gap in his company’s services. Instead of hanging back, he puts together a proposal and shares it with his manager. The idea gets the green light, and he’s picked to lead the project. That experience not only sharpens his skills—it builds his reputation as someone who takes initiative.
Most people don’t realize just how much control they actually have. They wait for instructions, or for someone else to set the agenda. But if you’re willing to ask, “How can I help?” or “What needs to be done?”—you’ll often find yourself right at the heart of brand new opportunities.
There’s another story that sticks with me—a group of friends who notice there’s a real need for affordable tutoring in their community. Instead of just talking about the problem, they organize free workshops at the local library. Before long, the program takes off, catching the attention of schools and local businesses. What started as a simple idea becomes a real movement, all because they decided to take action.
So, here’s the key takeaway—opportunity isn’t something you stumble across. It’s something you make. When you’re willing to take initiative, to offer help, and to jump in and solve problems, that’s what truly sets you apart.
